narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in this decision. The two strongest factors pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk, while one worked in your favor.

Your credit history of "no credits or all paid" was the most influential detail. This is quite rare—only 1% of approved applicants share this profile—making the bank view your repayment reliability as uncertain. Your requested loan duration of 36 months was the second most important factor. At nearly double the 19-month average of approved loans, this longer term increased the perceived risk. 

The amount you asked for actually helped your case. Although 3804 DM is above the typical approved loan of about 3020 DM, the model saw this specific request size as a moderate positive signal compared with other patterns in the data.

To improve your chances next time, focus first on building a clear track record of on-time payments on smaller credit products so your credit history shows steady, existing paid obligations. Consider applying for a shorter-term loan that stays closer to the 19-month average, and shop around for lenders who weigh credit history less heavily. Taking these steps should meaningfully strengthen future applications. (248 words)
